name: John Forbes Nash Jr.
milestone_by_age_26: Completed PhD at Princeton with dissertation 'Non-Cooperative Games' introducing the Nash equilibrium, a cornerstone of game theory and mathematical economics, at age 22 in 1950.
early_history_summary: Nash showed mathematical ability from age 14, entered Carnegie Institute of Technology at 16 on a Westinghouse Scholarship, and earned both BS and MS by age 20. He completed his PhD at Princeton in just two years, with his 27-page thesis introducing the Nash equilibrium concept that would later earn him the Nobel Prize in Economics.
family_context_summary: Father was an electrical engineer for the Appalachian Electric Power Company; mother was a schoolteacher. Middle-class family in Bluefield, West Virginia, who arranged supplemental education including advanced math courses at Bluefield College.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an electrical engineer and mother was a schoolteacher; parents arranged for him to take advanced mathematics courses at a nearby college during his final year of high school and encouraged his education.
primary_early_advantage_tags: elite university pipeline, mathematical prodigy, scholarship support, parental education emphasis
evidence_summary: Nash was recognized as a mathematical prodigy from his teenage years, entering Carnegie Tech at 16 on a full Westinghouse Scholarship and earning BS and MS degrees by 20. His parents, an electrical engineer and a schoolteacher, arranged advanced math courses during high school. At Princeton, he completed his PhD in two years, introducing the Nash equilibrium at age 22. The combination of elite institutional access (Carnegie Tech, Princeton) and extraordinary innate mathematical ability drove his early breakthrough.

name: Zaha Hadid

early_history_summary: Born in Baghdad to an upper-class Iraqi family, Hadid studied mathematics at the American University in Beirut before moving to London in 1972 to study architecture at the Architectural Association. She graduated in 1977 and joined the Office of Metropolitan Architecture before founding her own practice in 1980.
family_context_summary: Father was a wealthy industrialist and politician who co-founded the National Democratic Party in Iraq and served as minister of finance. Mother was an artist from Mosul.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a politician, economist, and industrialist; mother was an artist. Upper-class family with strong political and cultural connections in Iraq.
evidence_summary: Hadid came from an upper-class Iraqi family and studied at the Architectural Association in London, but her first built project and major competition win came well after age 26. She was still a student at age 26.

evidence_summary: Loach studied law at Oxford and worked in regional theatre before joining the BBC as a trainee director at age 27. His first directing work came after age 26, and his first feature film at 31.

name: Sheldon Lee Glashow
milestone_by_age_26: Ineligible: Glashow completed his PhD thesis at Harvard in 1958-59 (around age 26), but his Nobel-winning electroweak SU(2)xU(1) paper was written in spring 1960 (age 27-28). The PhD thesis on vector mesons was not the material milestone for which he is known.
early_history_summary: Glashow graduated from Bronx High School of Science in 1950 (classmate of Steven Weinberg), studied at Cornell, and pursued graduate work at Harvard under Julian Schwinger. He completed his PhD by 1959 and found the SU(2)xU(1) electroweak structure in 1960 at Niels Bohr's institute in Copenhagen.
family_context_summary: Parents were Jewish immigrants from Russia; father became a successful plumber. Middle-class family in New York. Older brothers were a dentist and a physician.
parent_family_domain_summary: Brother Sam interested him in physics at age 10 and helped equip a basement chemistry lab at age 15. Parents encouraged scientific inclinations despite not having university education themselves.
evidence_summary: Glashow studied at Bronx Science and Cornell before pursuing his PhD at Harvard under Schwinger. His Nobel-winning electroweak theory paper was written in 1960 at age 27-28, after age 26. The PhD thesis on vector mesons was completed around age 26 but was not the landmark contribution.

name: George Soros

early_history_summary: Born in Budapest to a Jewish family, Soros survived the Nazi occupation and moved to the UK in 1947. He moved to New York in 1956 to work in finance.
family_context_summary: Born to a prosperous non-observant Jewish family in Budapest; father was a lawyer and Esperanto author, mother's family operated a successful silk store. Family survived WWII using false identity papers.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a lawyer and well-known Esperanto author; family was prosperous before the war. Father's experience surviving WWI as a POW and navigating WWII with false papers instilled resourcefulness.
evidence_summary: Soros survived the Nazi occupation of Hungary, emigrated to the UK, and studied at LSE before moving to New York in 1956 for entry-level finance jobs. His major investing milestones came decades later, with his first hedge fund founded at age 39.

name: Adele
milestone_by_age_26: Released debut album '19' in January 2008 at age 19, which became one of the best-selling debut albums in UK history with top-five singles 'Chasing Pavements' and 'Make You Feel My Love'; won Grammy for Best New Artist at age 20.
early_history_summary: Adele attended the BRIT School for Performing Arts and Technology from age 14, where a classmate posted her demo on MySpace, leading to a record deal with XL Recordings at age 17. Her debut album '19' was released in January 2008 when she was 19, achieving immediate commercial and critical success.
family_context_summary: Raised by a single mother, Penny Adkins, in working-class London after her father left when she was 2. Her mother worked as a furniture maker and adult-learning activities organizer.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Mother took her to gigs and listened to music with her, but no professional music industry background.
primary_early_advantage_tags: BRIT School, MySpace demo, London music scene, vocal talent, working-class drive
evidence_summary: Adele grew up in working-class London raised by a single mother, with no family music industry connections. She attended the BRIT School for Performing Arts from age 14, where a demo posted on MySpace by a friend led to a record deal with XL Recordings at 17. Her debut album '19' (2008) released at age 19 became one of the best-selling debut albums in UK history. Her early success combined natural vocal talent, the BRIT School pipeline, and the MySpace digital distribution wave.

name: Toni Morrison

evidence_summary: Morrison grew up in a working-class Black family in Ohio, studied at Howard and Cornell, and taught at Howard University. Her first novel was published at age 39 in 1970, well after age 26.

name: Nana Mouskouri
milestone_by_age_26: Won first prize at the inaugural Greek Song Festival in 1959 at age 24 with 'Kapou iparhei i agapi mou' by Manos Hatzidakis, and won first prize again at the 1960 festival, establishing her as a major Greek recording artist by age 26.
early_history_summary: Mouskouri displayed musical talent from age 6 and began formal singing lessons at 12. She was accepted to the Athens Conservatoire at 16, studying classical music and opera for eight years before pivoting to jazz. She recorded her first song in 1957 and met composer Manos Hatzidakis in 1958, who wrote songs specifically for her that won the Greek Song Festival.
family_context_summary: Father worked as a film projectionist in a local cinema; mother worked as an usher at the same cinema. Working-class family in Crete and Athens; parents could not afford to support both daughters' music studies.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Parents worked in a cinema, not in music.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Athens Conservatoire, Hatzidakis mentorship, early specialization, festival wins, vocal talent
evidence_summary: Mouskouri grew up in a working-class family in Crete and Athens, with parents who worked in a cinema. She showed musical talent from age 6 and entered the Athens Conservatoire at 16, studying classical voice for eight years. After pivoting to jazz and meeting composer Manos Hatzidakis in 1958, she won first prize at the inaugural Greek Song Festival in 1959 at age 24. Hatzidakis wrote songs specifically for her that became her early hits, making her a recognized artist in Greece by age 26.

name: Stanisław Lem
milestone_by_age_26: Published his literary debut, the science fiction novella 'Człowiek z Marsa' (A Man from Mars), serialized in the magazine 'Nowy Świat Przygód' in 1946 at age 25.
early_history_summary: Lem grew up in Lwów in a wealthy Jewish family; his father was a laryngologist. Medical studies were interrupted by WWII, during which he survived the Nazi occupation using false papers and worked as a mechanic. After the war, he moved to Krakow, continued medical studies, and began writing fiction to earn money, debuting with 'Człowiek z Marsa' in 1946.
family_context_summary: Father was a wealthy laryngologist and former physician in the Austro-Hungarian Army; the family was Jewish and upper-middle-class in Lwów. The family lost all property during WWII and survived using false papers.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a medical doctor (laryngologist) with an extensive library of medical books that Lem read as a child, fostering his scientific imagination. Father's cousin was poet Marian Hemar.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father's scientific library, wartime survival, intellectual family, self-taught writing, post-war debut
evidence_summary: Lem grew up in a wealthy Jewish family in Lwów; his father was a laryngologist whose medical books fostered his scientific imagination. WWII interrupted his medical studies and the family lost everything, surviving under false papers while Lem worked as a mechanic. After the war, he moved to Krakow and began writing fiction for income, debuting with the SF novella 'Człowiek z Marsa' in 1946 at age 25. The war's adversity catalyzed his pivot from medicine to writing.

name: Georg Bednorz

evidence_summary: Bednorz studied crystallography at Münster and spent summers at IBM Zurich as a student, but his PhD and Nobel-winning research all came after age 26. He had just completed his undergraduate degree at age 26.
